newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, marks and yen close down.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, marks and yen close down.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed, but the tone in marks and yen could firm up in the near term as the U.S. dollar finishes its correction to the downside, traders and analysts said.

"I think the dollar will go down before it goes up again," said Rob Fullem, a currency analyst at NatWest Markets, adding that he is looking for the dollar to grind down to 1.6700 spot, which would lead March marks just shy of $0.6000.
Fullem said the U.S. bond market could drag down the dollar if bonds continue to react so poorly to signs of low inflationary pressures in a modestly growing economy.
Many traders were disappointed after the U.S. bond market sold off after the U.S. January Consumer Price Index (CPI) and remained weak following the U.S. January real earnings data.

Average real weekly earnings of U.S. workers fell 2.0 percent in January, the biggest drop in more than 23 years, while both the overall CPI and the core rate rose 0.1 percent, compared to average trade estimates for CPI rises of 0.3 percent and 0.1 percent, respectively.
After U.S. bond futures closed, the U.S. stock market sold off, adding to concerns about the U.S. asset markets, Fullem said.
In addition, the Bundesbank's comments on Wednesday could linger in the foreign exchange markets, traders said.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer told a German newspaper that the dollar should now stop rising, and that he hoped "this correction has now come to an end."
Tietmeyer's comments coincided with the Bundesbank's monthly report for February which said the mark's appreciation in early 1995 had more than reversed.
There was little immediate reaction to the comments, as Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke was quoted as saying a 1.70 and 1.75 spot level would not raise inflation in Germany.
In responding to a question by Reuters, a spokesman said Welteke welcomed the rise of the dollar, but said normalisation had now taken place.

While some traders said the Swiss franc was leading the mark lower, Fullem said the dollar's near-term direction against most currencies, including the mark, hinged on its relationship with the yen ahead of Japan's fiscal year-end on March 31.
After March 31, Fullem is looking for dollar/yen to rise to 130.00 spot.
"It really bucks the trend of naysayers who are looking for intervention," Fullem said. "But there are enough reasons (for a higher dollar/yen)."
Floor sources noted active spreading between Australian and Canadian dollar futures. One firm bought 1,000 March Australian dollar contracts and sold an equal amount of March Canadian dollars.

At the close, March yen was down $0.000042 at $0.008062, marks down $0.0045 to $0.5903, Swiss francs off $0.0066 to $0.6753, sterling was up $0.0096 to $1.6152, Can dollars down $0.0026 to $0.7364 and Aussie dollars up $0.0026 at $0.7675.
